newsitem.title: POLAND: U.S. bank, IFC may buy stake in Polish bank.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank, IFC may buy stake in Polish bank.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation, the financial arm of the World Bank, Shore Bank from Chicago and three U.S. funds may take a strategic stake in Poland's Bank Wlasnosci Pracowniczej (BWP), BWP president said.
Kazimierz Glowacki told Reuters BWP was completing a memorandum for the investors, and if it was accepted, the bank would start work on an ex-rights issue worth $10 million in two equal tranches.
"We are at the final stage of the investment memorandum and we hope it will be accepted by Shore Bank from Chicago and the IFC as the future strategic investors in BWP," Glowacki said.
He said the three investment funds, which would also buy BWP's shares were already operating in Poland, but declined to give their names.

BWP's current main shareholders are the Gdansk Refinery with a 26.1 percent stake, the Gdansk Repair Shipyard with another 26.1 percent, WBK with 9.3 percent and Bank Zachodni SA also with 9.3 percent.
After 11 months of 1996 the bank had a net profit of 1.2 million zlotys, 358 percent more than in 1995 and expects to raise its earnings to 1.5 million zlotys in 1997.
At the end of November it had a capital of 8.4 million zlotys and a balance sheet total of 76 million zlotys.
